messages:
alice (arch): quick follow-up from the model-versioning RFC — we glossed over pin semantics for long-lived private deployments. need to decide exact metadata shape.
ben (runtime): yeah, saw gaps. main questions: anchored vs floating pins, TTL, and a machine-readable compatibility fingerprint.
carla (prod): +1. also how rollouts express partial traffic shifts. ops needs a clear, deterministic behaviour when model binary is missing or incompatible.
dan (platform): can we keep one canonical fieldset for hosted/dedicated/private? platform logic prefers a single contract we can enforce at ingest time.
eva (research): for quality tracking we need an immutable artifact id (hash) + optional semantic version. humans want semver, runtime wants hash.
ben (runtime): suggestion: metadata fields: `model_id`, `version` (human), `commit_hash` (immutable), `pin_mode` (`anchored|floating|range`), `ttl_seconds`, `compat_hash`, `fallbacks`, `rollout_percent`.
carla (prod): show an example? short snippet please.
ben (runtime): ```json
{
  "model_id": "redwood/gpt-neox-20b",
  "version": "v2.4.1",
  "commit_hash": "a1b2c3d4",
  "pin_mode": "anchored",
  "ttl_seconds": 2592000,
  "compat_hash": "kvm-compat-v1",
  "fallbacks": ["redwood/gpt-neox-20b-quant"],
  "rollout_percent": 10
}
```
alice (arch): looks good. semantics we should clarify: anchored = absolute commit_hash match required; floating = accept newer compatible versions matching compat_hash; range = semver range (e.g., ^2.4).
dan (platform): important: if compat_hash matches but commit_hash differs we still allow request to route to latest compatible — but we must surface in console which concrete commit served.
carla (prod): and what about automatic rollback? should there be an `auto_rollback_on_error` boolean + `error_threshold`?
eva (research): yes, but tie rollback triggers to evaluation/quality signals not only 5xx. e.g., BLEU/drop in eval set or hallucination regression.
ben (runtime): implementation note: runtime uses `compat_hash` + capability bitmask. that lets us avoid fragile semver parsing at routing time.
alice (arch): +1 on capability bitmask. but for user-facing UX keep semver/range for clarity; translate to bitmask internally.
dan (platform): security/note: for private deployments we must allow policy to override `fallbacks` (customer may block fallback models). add `fallback_policy` enum: `allow|deny|require_approval`.
carla (prod): good call — add `audited_by` field or `approval_ticket` for enterprise change logs.
ben (runtime): small perf note: TTL should be optional; if absent runtime trusts pin indefinitely unless a rollout replaces it. for safety we can enforce a max TTL global.
alice (arch): next steps: I'll draft a concise schema PR with examples + migration plan. @dan can you check platform enforcement constraints? @ben please prototype how runtime maps semver/range to compat_bitmask.
dan (platform): on it. will post infra constraints and a migration checklist.
deploy-bot: canary:models/update v2.4.1 -> v2.5.0 started by carla at 1818005605 :truck: (status: canary 10%)
carla (prod): deploying a canary now to test rollback hooks. will report if we see any perf regressions.
alice (arch): thanks all. syncing this with the RFC follow-up doc and will ping eng-sre separately for incident playbook changes. :white_check_mark:
